summary: Frontend-only regression test of morts-entry.html offline-queue fix. All four requested behaviors verified: (A) A queued item with a bad token that returns 4xx is discarded from bbm-staff-offline-queue AND recorded in bbm-staff-lost-items, with the red top banner data-testid='staff-lost-items-banner' showing '⚠️ 1 entry didn't save — please re-enter (tap to dismiss)'. Tapping the banner clears both the localStorage lost list and removes the banner. (B) Genuine offline simulation via page.context.set_offline(True) with a Save click queues the request; the bottom pill data-testid='staff-offline-queue-banner' shows 'Offline — 1 item queued'; upon going back online and tapping the pill, drainQueue() runs and the item is successfully drained (queue emptied, no entry appears in lost-items because the real API accepted it). (C) Happy path: filling name + culls + Save on shed 2 produced 'Saved' text (green badge), no red lost banner appears, and localStorage stays clean. (D) Weigh Birds tab within morts-entry.html loads and renders shed inputs without JS errors. (E) Code inspection confirmed presence of `visibilitychange` and `pageshow` listeners calling drainQueue(), r.ok success check, r.status>=500 keep-retry, else discard+record path, and updateLostBanner/pushLostItem/LOST_KEY definitions (lines 266-293 of morts-entry.html). No console or page errors on load. Cleaned up 2 real test entries via DELETE /api/integrations/morts?farm=default&date=2026-09-22 (returned {ok:true,deleted:2}).
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct and minimal: r.ok gate for success, >=500 for keep-retry, else discard-and-record, matching the reported symptom's root cause exactly.

Lost-items list stores only {url, ts, reason} not the body payload — intentional and lightweight (banner is a count-based prompt to re-enter). Users cannot recover the original numbers from the banner; they must re-key. Acceptable per design (impossible-to-miss prompt is the goal), but worth mentioning: if desired, storing the body would let a future 'restore last lost entries' UX exist.
visibilitychange + pageshow drain-on-resume addresses iOS Safari's setInterval pause while backgrounded — good hardening.
Bottom offline pill is now clickable (drainQueue on click) with a clear cursor/pointer style would help discoverability, but functionally works.
